questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Crucial for choosing my study destination were language and culture. I wanted to improve my language skills in Spanish. I also wanted to learn more about different cultures and was particularly interested in the Latin American continent. I wanted to take advantage of learning from a different, non-Scandinavian academic environment, as both Bachelor and Master I studied in Scandinavia.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I very much enjoyed my study abroad experience. I learned a lot of new skills and met people from around the world. I am very grateful for this opportunity.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Some information was quite accessible, other information was difficult to gather. There, it helped that was in contact with other students from KU who went to the same exchange University. More information was available for Bachelor students, Master students were often not in the same information channels and neglected.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The International Office was always accessible, however, usually did not follow up on my requests for information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: A lot of information was accessible for Bachelor students, Master students were not granted the same access to information. Yet, there were guided tours, which were nice and helpful. But, there was not mentor programme or so organized from the University.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There are different companies/organizations that offer housing and events and trips for international students. Such as "Cholula Capital", "Travels Life", "Casa Leyender", or "Charro Housing".

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are different companies that offer housing. These are very affordable and offer a place to meet other international students and few Mexicans as well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are different housing offers that offer different services.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The platform did not work at times so I had to reach out to the international office many times.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There is a portal for the incoming students. Some functions were difficult to access. Later, we had to register for different courses, which was not very easy either.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There international office was helpful at times.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to register to all the courses I wanted. However, some interesting courses were offered on Saturdays.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It was difficult to find out the course syllabus. Even upon request for more information it was difficult.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Most courses were very nice and interesting. However, I had a teacher that repeatedly changed the deadlines and requirements for the assignments, which made it difficult to follow.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took courses at Masters level. Some courses content was repeatition of courses I had during my Bachelors.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UDLAP, there was mandatory attendance and classes at Masters levels were taught in the hybrid format. The class size was much smaller. There were usually weekly assignments.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: International Studies and Institutions, Trade Agreements in Emerging Economies, Regional Studies and Global Political Economy.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: International Studies and Institutions and Global Political Economy.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was very affordable

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were many sports and freetime activities at the University, with many sports faclities, like tennis courts, gym, and swimming pool on campus.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of Sports activities, dancing, and social events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Salsa classes and using the free sports facilties.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travels as much as possible! There are many things you can learn during it. There are many affordable travel opportunities during the weekends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Mexican society is very welcoming and open. It was fairly easy to adapt. However, many things work very different compared to Denmark, which one has to get used to first, such as security.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There are many organization such as "cholula capital" which organize many social events for international students. This made it very easy to get to know international and local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There were few cultural differences, such as security, or student life. In Denmark, it is much freer, whereas it is much more regulated in Mexico. Additionally, UDLAP is a very expensive privat University which reflects the inequalities of the country. This is very different to the University life in Denmark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The welcoming nature and openness of all Mexicans, which I very much appreciate.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the students to be open for new experiences, adventures, learn Spanish and travel as much as possible.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend making use of the organizations that host events for international students. They were very helpful and a place to meet lots of people.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part was to meet many new people and improve my Spanish.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was challenging experience University in Spanish and navigate every day challenges.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
